Maya K: ran a quick smoke of the new 7B-int8 bring-up under the rapid-sampling harness and saw a weird throughput cliff at ~32 concurrency. p95 spikes, tokens/s drops ~40%.
Jordan: can you paste the loadgen command you used? which runner binary?
Maya K: using runner v0.9.7-hotfix, config: --concurrency 32 --batch-window-ms 6 --kv-cache enabled --quant-profile int8-opt. command: `./loadgen --model rdlw/7b-int8 --mode throughput --clients 4 --concurrency 32 --duration 60s`
ci-bot: loadgen job started: job_id=lg-20260312-84a; logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/lg-20260312-84a
Sam: interesting. quick checklist: 1) is this reproduced on a cold start vs warmed KV cache? 2) any socket disconnects / retry storms? 3) batch-window at 6ms can cause micro-bursting under certain schedulers.
Maya K: cold start shows same cliff, warm run still has the drop but earlier. no obvious disconnects in the runner logs.
Jordan: paste the tail of the runner logs around the spike, especially any `batch_size` / `dispatch` lines.
Maya K: log snippet: ```
[runner] dispatching batch_size=1 duration_ms=3
[runner] dispatching batch_size=2 duration_ms=4
[runner] dispatching batch_size=8 duration_ms=45  <-- p95 balloon
[kvcache] hit_rate=0.12
[perf] tokens/s=3200
[perf] tokens/s=1900
```
Anita: kvcache hit_rate 0.12 is suspiciously low for a production-like prompt set. Are we seeding the harness with varied prompts? rapid-sampling sometimes increases prompt variety which kills prefix caching.
Leo: also check the scheduler quantum on the node. I saw similar behavior when the GPU driver preemption granularity is 20ms and our batch-window forces lots of tiny batches that then queue. You might end up with one big expensive batch (duration 45ms) blocking others.
Jordan: could be batch packing regression in v0.9.7. We changed the packer heuristics last week to be more aggressive to reduce cost, might be misfiring under int8 kernel latency variance.
Sam: try two experiments: 1) increase --batch-window-ms to 12 to let the packer form steadier batches, 2) force `--kv-cache-mode warm` to measure best-case. Compare p95 and tokens/s.
Maya K: running both now. also toggled `--compact-quant` off to see if int8 packing jitter is kernel-related.
ci-bot: experiment run queued as lg-20260312-84b. ETA ~12m.
Maya K: quick interim results: batch-window 12ms -> tokens/s steady at ~4000, p95 stable. kv-cache warm -> hit_rate 0.78 and tokens/s improves ~15%. compact-quant off -> no obvious change. so likely interplay of small windows + cold KV cache + packer heuristics.
Anita: that points to our cost/correctness tradeoff in the packer. Under small windows the packer sometimes emits a singleton small batch delayed until a larger batch forms, creating outliers. We need tighter SLAs in the packer heuristics and a fallback to immediate dispatch if latency risk rises.
Leo: from infra perspective we should also add a metric for "batch_duration_variance" and expose it in the smoke dashboard. right now we only track avg batch_size and avg duration. high variance hides spikes.
Jordan: agree. For the eval harness CI: add an alert when p95 > target OR batch_duration_variance > threshold. That will catch these regressions earlier. Also add a deterministic microreproducer harness that sends a frozen prompt set to force cache hits.
Sam: I'll open a GH issue linking the log snippet and add a small unit test for packer behavior under tiny batch windows.
Maya K: GH issue opened: #3124 - packer microburst under rapid-sampling + low kvcache hit; added repro script and log link.
ci-bot: GH Issue created: https://git.internal/redwood/runner/issues/3124 by Sam
Jordan: final ask: can we quantify the cost per token delta in the smoke run? Maya, can you push the run stats (tokens emitted, GPU-ms used, cost estimate) into the eval dashboard? we need to show how this packer regression increases $/token.
Maya K: yup. snapshot: run A (batch-window=6) tokens=2.2M gpu-ms=14000 est_cost=$0.84 -> $0.000381/token; run B (batch-window=12) tokens=2.8M gpu-ms=15000 est_cost=$0.90 -> $0.000321/token. ~15% worse cost under small window.
Anita: that's a meaningful regression for Dedicated customers running tight SLOs. Recommend we gate the packer heuristic change behind an experiment flag and roll back in stable for now.
Leo: I'll add batch_duration_variance to the console metrics and wire a short report to the smoke dashboard.
Jordan: Sam/Dev: please prioritize patch for packer fallback. Sam, can you attach the unit test to the issue?
Sam: on it, will PR today with test and a small revert flag.
Maya K: thanks all. leaving the lg runs up for 1h for traces. ping me if you want join reproducer. :thumbsup:
